22274-julia-and-her-romeo-a-chronicle-of:
Julia and Her Romeo is a chronicle of Castle Barfield from David Christie Murray's Schwartz. Murray opens in 1820, when Abel Reddy farmed his own land at Perry Hall End. The two great houses of the parish were built as far apart as their boundaries allowed. Their owners, the Reddys and the Mountains, were a sort of Capulets and Montagues, hating each other for generations.

Samson and Abel kept the ancient grudge in full force. Into that feud Murray sets Julia and her Romeo, young lovers on opposite sides. Shakespeare's pattern is worn openly and kindly. The tale is village romance with a feud for its engine, told in Murray's easy style.
50983-four-afoot-being-the-adventures-of:
Four Afoot is a boys adventure novel by Ralph Henry Barbour, with a 1906 date in the record. Its subtitle promises the adventures of the Big Four on the highway in the open. A frontispiece shows the boys swinging along a country road on Long Island. Barbour list in front names Four in Camp and Four Afloat as companion tales.

Walking tours give the four friends their stage, road by road and town by town. School sport fame followed Barbour, yet this set trades the field for the footpath. Weather, inns, strangers, and scrapes supply the turns of a summer tramp story. Boys of 1906 gained a wholesome outdoor tale in the Big Four series.
podcast-joerogan-AIZYucKOzhw:
Director Oliver Stone talks with Rogan, in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, about the cover-up he sees behind the JFK assassination. Stone's film JFK made him the most famous voice of the case for a generation. Decades later, he has not moved from his ground.

He lays out the points he trusts: the wounds, the witnesses, and the files still held back. Rogan asks why the story will not die and what full disclosure would change. The segment is a veteran storyteller's brief for the idea that the public was never told the whole truth about Dallas.
podcast-joerogan-xPbZ19A03Hw:
Billionaire Robert Bigelow talks UFOs with Joe Rogan in episode 1612 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Bigelow, who made his money in hotels and aerospace, spent years funding serious UFO research. He bought Utah's Skinwalker Ranch, a site famed for strange events, to study it.

Bigelow explains why a hard-headed businessman takes the phenomenon seriously. He describes the ranch research and the government contracts his company held on the topic. Rogan asks what Bigelow believes after decades of spending on the question. Money meets mystery here, and the money man speaks with unusual candor.
